test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some cars are bikes.

All bikes are trucks.

Some trucks are buses.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some trucks are cars.

II. All buses are cars.

III. Some cars are buses.

IV. All bikes are buses.

options.text: Only conclusions I and IV follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I, II and IV follow

solution:
The least possible venn diagram is shown below,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6cbfe4ef6640b428961401aaf4d46f361d9af697af89428f340358195407400.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some trucks are cars → **True** (Some cars are bikes and all bikes are trucks implies that some of those trucks which are bikes are also cars).

II. All buses are cars → **False** (Because there is no relation given between buses and cars, so it is possible but not definite).

III. Some cars are buses → **False** (Because there is no relation given between buses and cars, so it is possible but not definite).

IV. All bikes are buses → **False** (Because there is no relation given between bikes and buses, so it is possible but not definite).

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusion I follows"**.
